questions.q: What's the tradeoff between Import mode and DirectQuery mode in Power BI?
options: Import is fast but a refreshed copy; DirectQuery is always current but only as fast as the source's query engine
Import and DirectQuery are functionally identical
DirectQuery is always faster than Import in every case
Import mode requires a live connection to the source at query time
questions.explain: Every real Power BI deployment before Fabric had to accept one of these two tradeoffs.

questions.q: What makes Direct Lake mode genuinely different from both Import and DirectQuery?
options: Power BI reads the Delta table's actual Parquet files directly, without going through Spark or a SQL endpoint as an intermediate engine
It's just a faster version of DirectQuery with no other difference
It's just a more frequently refreshed version of Import mode
It requires converting the data to a completely different file format first
questions.explain: This combines Import's speed with DirectQuery's freshness — a real third option, not a compromise.

questions.q: Why is Direct Lake mode possible at all?
options: Delta's Parquet files are already columnar and already have a real schema, letting Power BI read them nearly as fast as its own Import format
Power BI secretly converts the Parquet files to its own format before every query
It only works because Fabric disables all other query engines
It requires the data to be stored as CSV instead of Parquet
questions.explain: This connects to Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 14's point about Parquet's columnar, schema-aware structure.

questions.q: Why does Direct Lake mode need Delta's transaction log specifically?
options: The _delta_log/ folder tells Power BI exactly which Parquet files currently belong to the table's latest version
The transaction log is irrelevant to Direct Lake mode
Direct Lake mode works identically on plain Parquet with no log at all
The log is only used for Import mode, never Direct Lake
questions.explain: This is the exact same mechanism from Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 17 that also enabled time travel and safe concurrent writes.

questions.q: How does Direct Lake mode relate to the concepts from Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 18 and 21?
options: It's a direct beneficiary of the same transaction log mechanism that made time travel and safe concurrent writes possible there
It has no relationship to those earlier lessons at all
It replaces the need for a transaction log entirely
It only works if time travel is explicitly disabled on the table
questions.explain: The same log-reading mechanism underlies all of these features, just applied to a new use case here.
